title: Annotatio IV §.XXIV: rebuttal (1) — private twisted comments; no more wound Reformed than Calixtus/Pietists wound Lutherans
pass_a_gloss: Which things the most Famous Man, to reconcile a certain appearance of injury done to the Reformeds’ company, adduces concerning an intentional and effective presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper remembered by some Reformed; concerning an absence of Christ’s body from the Sacred Supper acknowledged and sincerely professed by others (same §. 4); and fourthly so great a spherical distance of Christ’s Body from the Sacred Supper as the highest Heaven stands from earth, from Calvin, and on denying both illocal and local presence of Christ in the Supper (§. 5 from Trelcatius) — except that (1) these are Comments of private Authors abounding in their own sense, most of them twisted against their mind, as if they were opposed to every real presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper, which yet from their testimonies written into my little Tract stands openly otherwise: Certainly those things strike the Reformed Church no more (even if they were not twisted, having rather suffered something human and adverse to themselves) than the assertions of certain ones commonly coming under the name of Pietists or Syncretists — specially Calixtus, whose Authority the Author himself holds of slight moment among the orthodox (§. 20), as one who played not only with the Reformed but even with the Pontiffs, judged otherwise of the Lutheran Churches’ Symbols, and led some to desert the truth — will be seen to strike the Church which alone the Author holds orthodox and truly Lutheran.
pass_b_english: The Professor piles intentional/effective presence, some Reformed’s absence-language, Calvin’s heaven–earth distance, and Trelcatius on denying local/illocal presence — as if against every real presence.

Rebuttal (1): mostly private comments twisted against their authors’ mind. Even untwisted they wound the Reformed no more than Pietist/Syncretist (esp. Calixtus) assertions wound the Lutheran church the Professor alone calls orthodox.
source_text: Quæ Vir Clarissimus ad speciem quandam injuriæ, Reformatorum Cætui factæ, conciliandam, de intentionali & effectiva corporis Christi in S. Cœna præsentia, nonnullis Reformatis memorata; ab aliis corporis Christi agnita sinceréque professa à S. Cœna absentia; §. eodem 4tio; Quartò verò sphæra distantia Corporis Christi à Cœna S. tanta, quanta altissimum Cœlum à terra distat, ex Calvino, deque tàm illocali, quam locali Christi præsentia in Cœna neganda, §. 5. ex Trelcatio adducit, præterquam quòd (1) privatorum sensuque suo abundantium Auctorum Commenta sunt, pleraque contra mentem eorum detorta, quasi ista omni reali corporis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiæ opposita essent, quod tamen secus se habere ex testimoniis eorum, in Tractatulo meo adscriptis, in propatulo est: Certè, non magis Reformatam Ecclesiam ista feriunt (etiam si detorta non essent, humani potiùs aliquid passa sibi que ipsis adversa) quam Ecclesiam, solam Auctori orthodoxam vereque Lutheranàm habitam, ferire videbuntur asserta quorundam vel Pietistarum, vel Syncretistarum nomine vulgò venientium, speciatim Calixti, cujus Autoritatem exigui inter orthodoxos momenti esse Autor perhibet §. 20. ut qui non modò cum Reformatis, sed etiam cum Pontificiis, colluserit, de Symbolis Ecclesiarum Lutheranarum secùs judicaverit, & nonnullos ad deserendam veritatem adduxerit.
notes: Rebuttal (1): twisted private comments; Calixtus analogy.
